title: Versioned consent and eligibility
prompt:
Implement `evaluate_subject(subject, protocol, on)` in `trialops/eligibility.py`, returning `{"eligible": bool, "reasons": list[str], "consent_version": str | None}` for a synthetic screening workflow. `on` is a date. The subject has `birth_date` (ISO date), `consents` (list of `{version, signed_on}`), `labs` (name -> number), and `flags` (list of strings). The protocol has `min_age`, `max_age`, `required_consent_version`, `consent_valid_from`, `labs` (name -> inclusive `[low, high]`), and `exclusions` (flag strings). Require the latest signed consent at or before `on`; it must match the required version and be signed on/after `consent_valid_from`. Compute age exactly on `on`, include both age and lab boundaries, and evaluate exclusions by name. Deterministic reason order: `CONSENT_MISSING`, `CONSENT_VERSION`, `AGE_BELOW_MIN`, `AGE_ABOVE_MAX`, each `EXCLUSION_<FLAG>` in protocol order, then `LAB_<NAME>_LOW` or `LAB_<NAME>_HIGH` sorted by lab name. Return the selected consent version even when it is the wrong version. Missing/malformed required input raises ValueError naming the field, not a raw KeyError or datetime exception. Add tests for leap-day birthdays, same-day consent, retired/wrong consent, exact age/lab boundaries, and reason ordering.

The reference runtime is Python 3.11. Select the latest consent by signed_on across all versions, then assess that selected record; do not fall back to an older consent. Age and lab limits are inclusive. Inputs are date-only ISO strings; no timestamps, units, or lab series are involved.

title: Governance-driven research export
prompt:
Implement `export_subjects(subjects, *, purpose, secret, on)` in `trialops/privacy.py`, returning `{"rows": [...], "manifest": {"algorithm": "sha256", "count": N, "sha256": digest}}`. Input records have `id`, `name`, `birth_date`, `email`, `country`, `visits` (ISO dates), `consents` (list of `{purpose, signed_on, withdrawn_on?}`), and `purge_after`. Include a record only when it has a consent for `purpose` with signed_on <= on and (no withdrawal or withdrawal > on), and purge_after >= on. Pseudonym = first 16 lowercase hex characters of HMAC-SHA256(secret, `purpose + ':' + id`). Each row contains only `pseudonym`, `country`, `birth_year`, and chronologically sorted `visits`; sort rows by pseudonym. Never emit id, name, email, full birth date, consent records, purge_after, or the secret. Manifest digest = SHA256 of `json.dumps(rows, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False)` encoded as UTF-8. Inputs must not be mutated. Empty input is valid. Invalid dates or empty secret/purpose raise ValueError; exceptions must not echo any subject identifier or secret. Add tests for withdrawal/expiry boundaries, duplicate IDs (reject them), deterministic output, canonical hashing, and absence of direct identifiers throughout values and errors.

IDs must be ASCII strings matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`; all other IDs are invalid. Duplicate IDs raise ValueError with code `DUPLICATE_SUBJECT_ID`. HMAC key and message bytes are UTF-8 encodings of secret and `purpose + ":" + id`. Use an allowlist only. JSON serialization rejects NaN and infinity. Retention and consent boundaries are inclusive exactly as stated.

Additionally implement `execute_reuse_export(request, subjects, *, actor, secret, now)` as an integration with the governance workflow in `trialops/governance.py`. Keep `export_subjects` compatible. Delegate exactly once to `apply_reuse_action(request, 'execute', actor, now, executor=...)`; its executor calls `export_subjects` exactly once using the approved snapshot's purpose, the supplied secret, and the UTC date of `now`. Return the complete executed request with the unchanged export in `execution_result`. Governance failures must reject before consuming subjects. Export failures become `EXECUTION_FAILED` through governance and leave the approved request/history unchanged. Repeated execution raises `INVALID_STATE` without re-consuming subjects. Never expose the secret or direct subject identifiers in the returned request, history, or top-level exception messages. Add end-to-end and rollback tests.

title: Restore and continue audit chain
prompt:
Implement `AuditChain` in `trialops/audit.py`. `AuditChain()` starts with previous_hash = 64 zeroes. `append(*, event_id, actor, action, at, payload)` returns a record with `sequence` starting at 1, `event_id`, `actor`, `action`, `at`, `payload`, `previous_hash`, and `hash`. `at` must be timezone-aware; normalize it to UTC as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (microseconds rejected). Canonicalize payload with `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False)` and compute SHA256 over canonical JSON of every record field except `hash`, in normal key-sorted serialization. Reject empty event/actor/action strings and duplicate event IDs. `verify(records)` returns a deterministic list of error codes, not a boolean: valid/empty chains return []; detect bad sequence, previous_hash linkage, wrong record hash, duplicate event IDs, non-increasing timestamps, malformed timestamps/hashes, and non-dict payloads. Provide `GENESIS_HASH = '0' * 64`. Add tests for UTC offsets, payload key order, tampering, replay, gaps, and multiple independent chains. Do not add external dependencies.

Extend verification to `verify(records, *, expected_head=None, expected_length=None)`. `head()` returns the current head hash, or GENESIS_HASH for an empty chain. When supplied, expected_length must equal the number of records and expected_head must equal the last record hash (GENESIS_HASH for empty), with stable errors `LENGTH_MISMATCH` and `HEAD_MISMATCH`; otherwise perform the internal checks from the original prompt. Verification must not normalize stored timestamp representations. Canonical JSON uses allow_nan=False. This detects un-rehashed edits and, with the trusted head/length, rehashed edits and suffix truncation; no cross-chain replay guarantee is claimed.

Add `AuditChain.from_records(records, *, expected_head, expected_length)` for restoring a persisted snapshot. Both trusted arguments are required. Materialize the input once and validate it with `verify`, passing both trusted arguments. An empty snapshot is valid only with length zero and GENESIS_HASH. On verification errors, raise ValueError with exactly `INVALID_CHAIN:` plus the sorted error codes joined by commas. On success return an independent chain containing a deep copy of the records, with previous_hash and the duplicate-event-ID index restored. The next append uses sequence expected_length + 1 and the restored head. Existing append behavior is unchanged. Test restore-and-continue, restored duplicates, deep-copy independence, wrong anchors, truncated suffixes, and independent restored instances.

title: Eligibility-gated visit reservations
prompt:
Implement `plan_visits(*, first_day, offsets_months, hour, minute, timezone, closed_days=None, capacity=None)` in `trialops/scheduling.py`. Add calendar months using the original day clamped to each target month's last day (Jan 31 -> Feb 28 -> Mar 31). Offsets must be unique nonnegative integers. Build local datetimes in the IANA `timezone` using `zoneinfo`; reject invalid zones and out-of-range times. Visit days in `closed_days` or with remaining `capacity` of zero move forward to the next available day. `capacity` maps dates to positive remaining slots; multiple visits may compete for a slot but input mappings are not mutated. Keep protocol order in the returned list, each item `{"offset_months": n, "local": local_iso, "utc": utc_iso}` with seconds and UTC `Z`. Handle month-end/leap years, inclusive capacity boundaries, closures, DST gaps (move a nonexistent local time forward by the gap), and ambiguous times deterministically (fold=0). Preserve the original local wall time when moving to another day. Add tests for New_York spring-forward/fall-back, Paris, multi-visit capacity, and leap-year month ends.

The grading runtime is Python 3.11 with tzdata 2025.2 pinned. Use only fixed fixture zones America/New_York and Europe/Paris. Monthly candidates always derive from first_day, never from a previously clamped or rescheduled visit. Use earliest-feasible greedy allocation in protocol order. If no date is available within 366 days after the nominal candidate, raise ValueError with code `UNSCHEDULABLE` and do not return a partial plan or mutate capacity.

Add `book_subject_visits(subject, protocol, *, on, first_day, offsets_months, hour, minute, timezone, capacity, closed_days=None)` integrating eligibility with persistent reservations. `capacity` is a required caller-owned dict of date to nonnegative integer. Call `evaluate_subject(subject, protocol, on)` before planning. If ineligible, raise ValueError with `INELIGIBLE:` plus the ordered reasons and do not change capacity. Delegate all candidate generation, closure, DST, validation, and within-plan allocation to `plan_visits`. Only after complete success, decrement capacity entries for returned visit days and return the unchanged list. Decrement only dates already present; unlisted dates retain unconstrained behavior and are never inserted. Any failure leaves capacity exactly unchanged, while earlier successful calls remain committed. Never mutate subject, protocol, or closed_days. Test sequential slot contention, later-visit rollback, ineligible subjects, and preserved DST/month-end behavior.

title: Safety follow-up triage
prompt:
Implement `triage_events(events, *, now)` in `trialops/safety.py` for fictional safety-event follow-ups, not medical judgment. Events have `event_id`, `subject_pseudonym`, `event_code`, `onset` (timezone-aware ISO datetime), `seriousness` (`fatal`, `life_threatening`, `hospitalization`, or `other`), `source`, optional `follow_up_of`, and optional `uncertain` boolean. Merge each follow-up chain into one case: reject duplicate IDs, missing roots, cycles, or a chain mixing subject pseudonyms/event codes. Output one dict per case with `case_id` (root ID), `subject_pseudonym`, `event_code`, `onset` (earliest UTC ISO with Z), `seriousness` (highest by fatal > life_threatening > hospitalization > other), `report_by` (earliest onset + 7 days for fatal/life_threatening, 15 for hospitalization, 30 for other), `sources` (sorted unique), `event_ids` (sorted), and `uncertain` (true if any event has it). Sort cases by onset then case_id. `now` must be aware and is used to add `overdue` when report_by < now. Preserve all source IDs and uncertainty; never invent a diagnosis. Add tests for chained follow-ups, offsets, duplicate roots, cycles, mixed codes, seriousness precedence, and overdue boundaries.

Input order must not affect output. Deadline clocks are based on earliest onset, not follow-up arrival time. Unknown seriousness, naive timestamps, and invalid event links raise ValueError with stable codes. Overdue is strictly report_by < now; equality is not overdue. Do not implement fuzzy matching or real reporting rules.

title: Data-reuse approval workflow
prompt:
Implement `apply_reuse_action(request, action, actor, now)` in `trialops/governance.py`. The request dict has `id`, `requester`, `reviewer`, `purpose`, `status` (`draft`, `submitted`, `approved`, `rejected`, `executed`, `expired`), `retention_until` (ISO date), `pseudonymized` (bool), `metadata` (`representative` and `complete` booleans, `quality_score` number), and `history` list. Deep-copy inputs; never mutate the caller. Actions: `submit` (requester only, draft -> submitted); `approve` (reviewer only, submitted -> approved, sets `approval_expires_on` = now + 30 days); `reject` (reviewer only, submitted -> rejected); `execute` (requester only, approved -> executed); `expire` (any actor, approved/submitted -> expired when now > approval_expires_on if approved, otherwise now > retention_until). Every action appends `{action, actor, at}` to history, with aware `now` normalized to UTC Z. Approval requires requester != reviewer, pseudonymized=True, representative and complete metadata, quality_score >= 0.95, now <= retention_until, and a nonempty purpose. Execution requires approved status, actor=requester, now <= approval_expires_on, now <= retention_until, and all the same privacy/metadata checks. Invalid role transitions raise PermissionError; invalid states or failed checks raise ValueError with stable machine-readable codes (`INVALID_STATE`, `SELF_REVIEW`, `PSEUDONYMIZATION_REQUIRED`, `METADATA_REQUIRED`, `APPROVAL_EXPIRED`, `RETENTION_EXPIRED`). Add tests for separation of duties, deep-copy behavior, stale approvals, missing metadata, failed execution, and history chronology. This is a synthetic workflow, not a compliance implementation.

Replace the `pseudonymized` boolean with `privacy_plan`: `{"algorithm": "hmac-sha256", "domain": purpose, "fields": ["pseudonym", "country", "birth_year", "visits"]}` exactly. Extend the signature to `apply_reuse_action(request, action, actor, now, executor=None)`. Execute requires a callable executor; call it exactly once with a deep copy of the approved request and store its returned dict as `execution_result`. If it raises, raise ValueError with code `EXECUTION_FAILED`, leave status approved and history unchanged, and never report executed. Repeated execution fails as INVALID_STATE without another executor call. Approval and execution require the exact privacy plan, not a boolean. All actions are atomic: no state/history mutation on failure.
